answers.question: The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?
answers.answer:
No, there is no room for a 22-miler, and chasing one now would cost more than it gives. Here is the reasoning.

- The race is 3 weekends away. Your last long run should land 2 weeks before the race, which means one more big Sunday (this one) and then a shorter one next weekend.
- The fitness from a 22 wouldn't show up by Oct 18; it takes about 3 weeks to absorb a long run. What you add now, you race tired on.
- You already have one 20 and a strong 17 in the bank, plus solid weekly volume. That is enough endurance for sub 3:45.
- The useful stress now is specificity, not distance. Sunday is 20 mi with 8 mi at goal marathon pace (around 8:35/mi) in the middle. That rehearses pace, fueling and legs under fatigue, which is what race day actually asks of you.

Trust the build. The work is done; the next 3 weeks are about sharpening and arriving fresh.

new.analysis:
## Where you are

You executed the week of Sep 21 – 27 exactly as planned: easy days easy, threshold on target with low fade, and 17 mi long run at 9:59/mi with only +4.7 bpm drift. That is a confident peak-phase week, and it tells me the engine is ready.

## Why this week looks the way it does

This is the last week where we add race-specific stress before the taper. Wednesday is a marathon-pace block, not threshold, because the question Oct 18 asks is whether 8:35/mi feels sustainable, not whether you can run faster for short reps. Sunday rehearses the same pace inside a long run so your legs learn it under fatigue.

## About the mileage worry

Marathons are won on consistency, not on one hero session. You have strung together steady 40+ mi weeks, a 20, and clean workouts; that is the resume that gets you to sub 3:45. From here, more miles hurt more than they help.

## What to watch on Sunday

Warm up for about 4 easy miles, run 8 mi at 8:30 – 8:40/mi, then finish easy. If heart rate climbs past the mid-160s during the marathon-pace block, hold the pace and note it; we will use that to set race-day effort. Practice your race fueling (gels, fluids) on this run; it is your dress rehearsal.
